    AI Overview
    Tiger Woods has won the Masters Tournament five times. His victories occurred in 1997, 2001, 2002, 2005, and 2019. He is second all-time in Masters wins, trailing only Jack Nicklaus, who has six. 
    • 1997: First Masters win at age 21, breaking the record for youngest champion and winning by a record 12 strokes.
    • 2001: Secured his second title, completing the "Tiger Slam" by holding all four major championship trophies simultaneously.
    • 2002: Won his second consecutive Masters, becoming the third player to repeat as champion.
    • 2005: Won in a playoff against Chris DiMarco.
    • 2019: Captured his fifth title, marking his first major win in 11 years following multiple back surgeries.

    People also ask
    Who has won the Masters the most?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Jack Nicklaus holds the record for the most Masters tournament wins, securing six Green Jackets during his career (1963, 1965, 1966, 1972, 1975, 1986). Tiger Woods is second with five victories, followed by Arnold Palmer with four. 
    Most Masters Wins (All-Time) 
    • 6 — Jack Nicklaus (1963, 1965, 1966, 1972, 1975, 1986)
    • 5 — Tiger Woods (1997, 2001, 2002, 2005, 2019)
    • 4 — Arnold Palmer (1958, 1960, 1962, 1964)
    • 3 — Jimmy Demaret, Sam Snead, Gary Player, Nick Faldo, Phil Mickelson 
    Key Records 
    • Most Wins: Jack Nicklaus (6).
    • Back-to-Back Wins: Only three players have defended their title successfully: Jack Nicklaus (1965-1966), Nick Faldo (1989-1990), and Tiger Woods (2001-2002).
    • Oldest Winner: Jack Nicklaus won his sixth title at age 46 in 1986.
    • Youngest Winner: Tiger Woods won his first title at age 21 in 1997.
